chunks.title: CLO Tips Workshop - Seamless Fitting Technique Production
chunks.content: ## Seam Line Minimization on Non-Woven Fabric This section explains techniques for minimizing visible seam lines on non-woven fabric using a sewing machine, including stitching adjustments and seam line manipulation to achieve a smooth, even finish. To reduce seam visibility on non-woven fabric, first sew all seams using a sewing machine. Then, adjust the machine’s stitch strength to zero on the right side of the machine. Next, switch the tool to adjust the seam line, which effectively eliminates the visible seam line on the fabric surface. When pressing the fabric, select the seam lines on both sides and open the seam to a width of 6 mm. The seam line type should be chosen based on the desired visual effect; if the seam line is too thick, it will not fit properly. Set the inner seam line to 6 mm as well, ensuring alignment and consistency. For visualization, enable direct rendering and simulation by clicking on a blank area and using the control key to open the simulation view. This allows inspection of the effect of pressure glue filling the seam gap, improving the seam’s appearance and structural integrity. --- ## Handling Seam Gaps and Sleeve Construction This section covers managing seam gaps, setting seam widths, and producing sleeve components using consistent seam allowance techniques. After completing the initial seam adjustments, hide the platform view to better observe seam gaps. The gap positions vary; it is critical not to select extension bars during this process, as this can cause unwanted extension to the bottom edge of the pattern board. Similarly, deselect and extend internal lines as required to control seam positioning. The width of these gaps is adjustable; for example, a gap width of 12 mm is used in this demonstration. The lower and bottom boards of the sleeve are constructed similarly. Adjust the bar width according to design needs, ensuring the internal seam line width and bar width remain consistent. The height of the bottom board should also match these specifications. Seam allowance is completed on one side of the transparent pattern piece, then mirrored on the opposite side using the same method. This ensures symmetry and continuity across the chest and sleeve pieces. --- ## Collar Seam Allowance and Shape Adjustment This section details the process of adding seam allowance to the collar and adjusting collar shape parameters to achieve proper fit and visual alignment. Begin by creating seam allowance on the collar similar to previous steps. Identify the string, width, and size parameters of the shirt collar. Select the two outer threads of the seam allowance on the large body collar and flip to the back side for further adjustments. The collar shape requires fine-tuning to receive the intended form. The large body collar’s edges face outward, and angle measurements are critical: straight edges have 30% greater length than 180%, while the side angle is approximately 240%. These percentages refer to relative curvature and stretching properties.

chunks.content: Identify the string, width, and size parameters of the shirt collar. Select the two outer threads of the seam allowance on the large body collar and flip to the back side for further adjustments. The collar shape requires fine-tuning to receive the intended form. The large body collar’s edges face outward, and angle measurements are critical: straight edges have 30% greater length than 180%, while the side angle is approximately 240%. These percentages refer to relative curvature and stretching properties. If the collar line is not visually prominent enough, adjust the intensity of the shape deformation by increasing it slightly to enhance the collar’s contour and fit. --- ## Summary of Seam Allowance Workflow in CLO This final overview highlights the overall workflow for producing seamless garment components in CLO software, emphasizing seam allowance creation, gap management, and shape adjustment: - Sew seams with the machine, then reduce stitch strength to zero to eliminate seam lines. - Adjust seam lines to 6 mm width and select appropriate seam types for fit and appearance. - Use direct rendering and simulation to preview pressure glue effects filling seam gaps. - Control gap widths (e.g., 12 mm) and avoid unwanted extensions by careful selection of pattern elements. - Maintain consistent seam allowance widths across sleeve boards and chest pieces. - Apply seam allowance to collars, then fine-tune collar shape using angle and intensity adjustments for optimal fit. This method ensures a smooth, professional finish on non-woven fabrics, suitable for detailed garment fitting and production in CLO.
